title: Unified Multi-Domain Graph Pre-training for Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Graphs via Domain-Specific Expert Encoding

problem.claim: Existing graph pre-training methods generally target either homogeneous or heterogeneous graphs, limiting unified modeling across graph types.

gap.claim: A unified approach must address mixed graph types and distribution shifts between pre-training and deployment, including cross-domain discrepancies caused by mixed graphs.

contributions.claim: GPH2 is a unified multi-domain graph pre-training method for homogeneous and heterogeneous graphs.
Unified Multi-View Graph Construction encodes homogeneous and heterogeneous graphs without explicit graph-type-specific designs.
Domain-specific expert encoding independently pre-trains experts on individual graphs, and Task-oriented Expert Fusion adaptively integrates experts according to discriminative strengths.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that a balanced mixture of homogeneous and heterogeneous graph pre-training benefits downstream tasks.
The authors report extensive experiments on mixed graphs showing stable transfer across graph types and domains.
The authors report that GPH2 significantly outperforms existing graph pre-training methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph pre-training provides transferable representations for downstream adaptation.
Existing methods separate homogeneous and heterogeneous graph modeling despite mixed real-world graph settings and distribution shifts.
The paper proposes GPH2 and a unified multi-view construction for jointly handling both graph types.
Domain-specific experts and task-oriented fusion address cross-domain discrepancies and combine experts for downstream tasks.
Experiments on mixed graphs are reported to show stable transfer and improved performance over existing methods.

source_observation.claim: The method independently pre-trains experts on individual graphs and adaptively fuses them for downstream tasks.

interpretation.claim: Separating domain-specific representation learning from downstream expert integration may help manage cross-domain discrepancies.

application.claim: For systems spanning heterogeneous data domains, consider domain-specific components with task-dependent integration.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when expert separation is preferable to a single shared encoder.

unknowns: Specific datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
The abstract does not describe the architecture or training objectives in detail.
The conditions under which the balanced mixture benefits downstream tasks are unspecified.
